svg.title: Ontology-based multi-source host APT architecture
svg.desc: Four layers describe meta-models, shared ontologies, domain ontologies and proposed deployment. Multi-source host logs, endpoint modules, central VM services, persistent storage and a gated model lifecycle are distinguished. This is a target conceptual ontology, not an implemented OWL reasoner.
svg.text: ONE CENTRAL VM · MULTIPLE SERVICES / CONTAINERS
PERSISTENT STORAGE / MOUNTED VOLUME · LOGICAL STORES
LogRecord observedBy LogSource; Process runsOn Host
Process spawns Process; Event targets Resource
Endpoint observations retain their source origin
These source types are subclasses of LogSource
Adapters map source fields to shared concepts
Collect evidence → send logs and scores
Agentic investigation is an optional extension
Align prediction targets and available evidence
Unknown cases → review, not automatic labels
Evaluate on held-out old and new domains
Versioned rollout to eligible model services
Ontology-based Architecture for Multi-source Host APT Detection
Target conceptual design • semantic relationships and deployment mapping
Proposed system; ontology specification, endpoint integration and learning lifecycle require implementation.
Services instantiate these concepts; source adapters and schema checks enforce the mappings.
UPDATE TRIGGER: sustained drift OR reviewed degradation OR sufficient confirmed new samples
Controller gates the request; drift alone never supplies ground-truth labels.
Logical responsibilities may share a container. Container placement is a deployment choice.
Schema / ontology mappings are versioned with adapters, datasets and model metadata.
Current Lam benchmark uses Zeek-derived flow features; endpoint-only inputs need new adapters, retraining and validation.
Grey: semantic mappings · Amber dashed: proposed data exchange · Red: learning / deployment control · All runtime integration is proposed.
